title: An event queue
description:
Let systems talk through a queue of events instead of calling each other.

```
physics: posts Collision(1, 2)
combat:  reads Collision(1, 2) -> posts Damage(2, 10)
audio:   reads Damage -> plays "hit"
events this frame: 2; next frame: 0
```
hints: A `std::variant` (from `<variant>`) holds exactly one of several types at a time: `using Event = std::variant<Damage, Heal>; Event e{ Damage{ 5 } };`. `std::get_if<Damage>(&e)` returns a pointer to the `Damage` inside, or `nullptr` if `e` holds something else, so `if (const auto* d{ std::get_if<Damage>(&e) }) { ... }` handles one type.
Swap the queue into a local vector before dispatching, so new events go into the empty one (lesson 10.03).
`std::visit` with an overloaded lambda, or `std::get_if<Damage>(&e)`, finds the type.
requirements: Events are a `std::variant` of a few structs.
Systems subscribe to the types they care about; the queue dispatches at one point in the frame.
Events posted while dispatching run next frame, not in the same loop.
stretch: Give events a delay so some run a number of frames later.
